source_snapshot.procedure: Generic setup says clear logs; display and check security logs; use `Save Logs`; then use `Clear All Logs`.
source_snapshot.criteria: Information/messages match status; security logs export and clear successfully.
source_snapshot.deepseek: YES supplies one assumed, possibly paginated Redfish GET with disabled TLS verification; it omits the required WebUI, export and clear actions and incorrectly claims no risk.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION separates read/export from destructive clear, rejects pre-clearing, and requires a complete retained baseline, exact service scope, retention authority and post-clear proof.

old_problem: The source orders a blanket evidence-destroying pre-clear before it checks and exports security records, then requests a second clear. Service identity, protected record classes, export completeness, retention authority and vendor post-clear semantics were not supplied, so the historical record retained a source conflict and decision Pending.
disposition_reason: The review decision is complete without inventing an OEM endpoint: retain the security-log viewer, Save Logs and Clear All Logs as separate checkpoints; reject blanket pre-clear under ED-17; bind the exact SecurityLog implementation, event matrix and retention contract at runtime; preserve a complete verified external export; and require fresh scope-specific authorization immediately before one irreversible clear. Project values affect execution readiness, not the review-layer method.
decision_basis: XLSX row 860, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, selection manifest and historical record were directly reviewed.
Security viewer correctness, complete export integrity/custody and destructive clearing are independent checkpoints; one Redfish Entries response cannot substitute for any other checkpoint.
ED-17 requires evidence preservation before BMC/SEL deletion; security records additionally require retention ownership and controlled custody.
ED-20 preserves all original viewer/export/clear coverage; ED-35 rejects read-only API substitution; ED-38 requires an exact target, approval, recovery and no automatic retry.

test_case.test_name: Verify Security Logs viewer, complete protected Save Logs export, and one explicitly authorized scoped clear
test_case.purpose: Prove the identified BMC Security Logs view presents the complete approved security-event set with correct message, actor, result/status, severity and time semantics; prove `Save Logs` creates a complete, usable, protected artifact; then, only on an authorized disposable lab BMC after independent export verification and a fresh explicit approval, invoke exactly one `Clear All Logs` action and prove it affects only the approved clearable SecurityLog scope while required audit markers and excluded services remain intact.
required_package: Exact lab BMC/controller/certificate, firmware/WebUI build, account role, maintenance window and authoritative SecurityLog service identity
Approved event matrix covering event type, actor/source, action, result/status, severity, message, timestamp/timezone, ordering, visibility, pagination, stable ID/sequence and concurrency
Vendor rules for retention/wrap/tamper behavior, immutable versus clearable classes, Clear All scope and any self-auditing clear marker or new sequence boundary
Save Logs filename, trusted origin, MIME/container, encoding/schema, all-page semantics, parser, checksum/signature, redaction and encrypted external custody policy
Written security/compliance retention decision, dedicated non-production target, exact one-time clear method, explicit clear authority and excluded-service observer list
Protected credentials, trusted TLS, supported UI/API client versions, alternate OOB access and incident escalation for wrong-scope or unrecoverable evidence loss
test_case.test_command: Do not perform the generic pre-clear. Discover the supported SecurityLog service and record its identity/schema. Capture every page and service metadata through trusted protected read access; correlate stable record IDs, actors, actions, messages, results/statuses, severities and timestamps with the complete WebUI view and approved matrix. Invoke the WebUI `Save Logs` once; isolate, parse, hash or verify the artifact and reconcile its IDs/count/sequence/time bounds with the complete baseline before placing it in approved external custody. Present the immutable target/service, clearable classes, verified artifact/checksum/location, excluded services, expected marker and stop conditions, then obtain fresh explicit approval. Invoke the exact `Clear All Logs` control once; verify old clearable entries are removed according to vendor semantics, the expected audit marker/new boundary exists, and excluded Audit/SEL/system services remain unchanged. Preserve all action evidence. Never use `curl -k`, command-line reusable passwords, assumed `/Managers/bmc/LogServices/SecurityLog`, blanket clear or automatic retry.
test_case.expected_result: The Security Logs WebUI and complete reference set agree with the approved security-event matrix. The Save Logs artifact is trusted-origin, readable, structurally valid, complete and protected in approved external custody. After fresh exact-scope approval, one clear affects only the authorized clearable SecurityLog records and reaches the vendor-defined post-state, including any required clear audit marker or new sequence boundary; excluded services and the retained export remain intact. No blanket pre-clear, credential leak, TLS bypass or repeated destructive action occurs.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires complete viewer-to-reference correlation, verified full export before deletion, custody evidence, recorded immediate approval, exactly one scoped clear, vendor-defined post-clear state and proof excluded/protected records remain, followed by an authorized engineer verdict. A single JSON response, UI toast, browser file presence, unexplained empty page or zero count without export completeness and scope proof cannot pass. Field mismatch, incomplete or unreadable export, wrong/multiple clear, protected evidence loss, absent required marker, unknown response or unexpected cross-service change is FAIL. Missing service/event/retention/clear contract or approval is NOT READY, not Pending or PASS.
safety_gate: Never perform the source's blanket pre-test clear; it destroys the records needed to verify viewer and export behavior and may violate security or legal retention.
Do not clear production, shared, incident-active or retained SecurityLog data. Use only the exact dedicated lab target and clearable class authorized in writing.

Before clear, enumerate all pages, validate and checksum/sign the export, place it in approved external custody and independently verify its completeness; a local browser download alone is not recovery.
Do not assume ManagerId, LogServiceId, endpoint, privilege or a zero-entry post-state. Bind vendor semantics, including a clear action that may immediately create its own security/audit record.
Protect usernames, addresses, authentication results and administrative actions; use trusted TLS and protected credentials, and redact display evidence without altering retained originals.

Invoke the exact approved clear once and never retry automatically. Stop on partial export, retention conflict, unclear scope, unexpected deletion, unknown response or unavailable excluded-service proof.
expected_evidence: BMC/controller/certificate, firmware/WebUI build, role and discovered SecurityLog service/schema identity
Approved security-event field/status/severity/actor/time/order/visibility matrix plus pagination, retention, tamper, clearable-class and marker rules
Complete pre-clear paginated raw set and redacted WebUI evidence reconciled by stable IDs/count/sequence/time boundaries
Save Logs trusted-origin metadata, filename, MIME/container, size, parser result, checksum/signature, completeness reconciliation and external custody/access record
Written retention/clear authority and fresh exact-action approval, single clear request/response, before/after boundary/marker and excluded-service preservation
Protected audit trail, no retry, incident/recovery status, limitations and authorized engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: The verified externally retained export and protected excluded-service observers are the pre-clear recovery controls; deleted BMC security records may not be restorable. If scope or response is wrong, stop immediately, preserve all request/response and audit evidence, isolate the controller and follow only the approved vendor/OOB incident path. Escalate any protected evidence loss and never recreate or fabricate records.

source_conflict.reason: ED-17 resolves the contradictory setup by preserving the original pre-clear text historically but prohibiting its execution; representative existing records are viewed/exported first, and only the separate final clear checkpoint may run after verified custody and fresh authorization.

blocked.reason: The three functional checkpoints and safe order are identifiable. OEM service IDs, event matrix, retention contract and clear semantics are required execution bindings and approvals, not unresolved review logic.
